A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MARS framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original MLE-Bench evaluations, component ablations, search analyses, lesson-utilization measurements, and computational costs.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds comparative-memory controls, harder-task ablations, Claude evaluations, lesson audits, and reduced-budget results.

M1.justification: v1 already compares new solutions with the current best when distilling lessons. Renaming Section 4.3 from Lesson Learning to Comparative Reflective Memory emphasizes this existing mechanism. The modular pipeline, MCTS procedure, Algorithm 2, and appendix prompts remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 75-competition MLE-Bench coverage. Added model and budget experiments reuse its Lite, Medium, and High tasks; lesson audits and case studies examine outputs from that coverage. No new benchmark domain or task environment is introduced.

E2.justification: v3 Figure 3b adds an empirical-analysis-only reflective-memory comparator, isolating comparison against the best-known solution. The existing no-memory variant is retained under revised terminology. AIDE, AIRA-dojo, leaderboard comparators, and search-strategy comparators remain.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 and Table 6 revise MARS+ hardware from two A100 GPUs and 24 vCPUs to two H100 GPUs and 48 vCPUs. New protocols include Claude 4.6 Sonnet evaluation on ten tasks per difficulty split, ten-task Medium/High ablations, a four-hour MARS budget, and audits of 3,611 lessons plus 20 manually inspected examples.

E4.justification: v3 adds a control isolating comparative reflection, extends component ablations beyond Lite to sampled Medium and High tasks, audits lesson attribution, and supplies two explanatory case studies. The four-hour cost comparison additionally tests whether useful performance requires greater spending. The penalty-weight sensitivity study already existed in v1 Appendix E.2 and is relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions use three independent runs and mean ± SEM for benchmark comparisons; the new Claude table follows this practice. No revised seed policy, run-count increase, confidence-interval method, or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Under revised hardware, MARS+ overall Any Medal changes from 59.6 ± 1.2% to 62.7 ± 0.8%, and Gold from 30.7 ± 1.3% to 33.8 ± 0.4%; these are not same-setting gains. Standard MARS and baseline table scores are retained. New results include Claude-subsample Any Medal rates of 55.6% versus AIRA-dojo's 20.0%, four-hour MARS achieving 28.4% at $9.6, and lesson-audit accuracies of 88.34% and 90%.

T1.justification: The problem definitions, optimization objectives, reward normalization, UCT expression, and update equations remain unchanged, including Equations 1–8. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution now explicitly frame complex MLE as the execution bottleneck addressed within automated AI research, qualifying the broader framing. The three central components, open-source MLE-Bench performance claim, and 63% cross-branch lesson-transfer claim remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix A explicitly limits demonstrated applicability to MLE-Bench and discusses computational expense and hallucinated causal attribution. Added discussions interpret the memory control, lesson audit, harder-task ablations, model transfer, and reduced-budget comparison as evidence for causal learning and architectural efficiency. These substantially expand both interpretation and qualifications.

D1.justification: Table 6 revises the MARS+ hardware specification, and Table 11 adds API-call, token-consumption, and pricing details for four-hour runs. Core hyperparameters, complete agent prompts, generated example code, and repository access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning across automated research, budget-aware tool use, and agent memory. New citations include AI Scientist, PiFlow, Agent Laboratory, DeepScientist, and ExpeL. It adds specific distinctions between integrated MCTS rewards and external budget mechanisms, and between code-level reflection and high-level trajectory comparisons.

P1.justification: Editing is concentrated in the opening framing, related work, renamed memory section, component-specific ablation discussion, and cost discussion. Appendices are reorganized to accommodate additions, but the main section sequence and extensive method, prompt, and code passages remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 reorganizes separate component, search, and appendix sensitivity plots into a four-panel main ablation figure, and adds corresponding four-panel Medium/High figures. It adds the Claude comparison table and expands the cost table with budget-labelled columns. Existing overview, trajectory, reward, and originality displays are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the central architectural claims: the comparative-memory control isolates a previously untested component, harder-task and Claude experiments test generality, and the four-hour comparison addresses whether gains require higher spending. Explicit limitations improve calibration. The lesson audit still does not establish causal proof, and Section 5.2 retains an obsolete highest-Gold claim for standard MARS, but these reporting weaknesses do not outweigh the stronger experimental support.
